verbatim_spans.text: ! to assure symmetric, use locally constant dx and dy

unresolved: In non-CARTESIAN DERIVATIVE_YY_HIGH, the last positive-y stencil sample at L407 is Uin(I+2,J+2), while the Cartesian counterpart at L404 and every other yy term keep I fixed; this diagonal I+2 copy/paste term changes the operator and can also exceed the x stencil range unexpectedly.

DERIVATIVE_Y_High coefficients at L68-L72 are [1,2,0,-2,-1]/(8 DY), and DERIVATIVE_X_High uses the same pattern at L104-L108. Their cubic moment is nonzero, so these named higher-order first derivatives retain O(h^2) truncation error rather than the fourth-order centered coefficients used elsewhere in this file.

All ten Uout dummy arrays are INTENT(OUT) but only Ibeg:Iend by Jbeg:Jend is assigned inside each routine; Fortran makes the entire incoming actual argument undefined on entry, so output cells outside that loop range remain undefined despite retaining full M-by-N shape.
Wide routines read I or J offsets of plus/minus two at L68-L72, L104-L108, L315-L335, L368-L372, and L403-L407 without checking that the supplied Ibeg/Iend/Jbeg/Jend leave two valid halo cells.
Every formula divides by DX, DY, DX(I,J), or DY(I,J), including squared products in second derivatives, without a nonzero spacing check.

Comments call DERIVATIVE_XY_HIGH, DERIVATIVE_XX_HIGH, and DERIVATIVE_YY_HIGH fourth derivatives at L293,L345,L381, but their formulas compute mixed or pure second derivatives with wider accuracy stencils.
